nodes.label: Game Developer

nodes.label: Correct Seam
nodes.rationale: A regression test is only worth writing where a seam exists that exercises the real bug pattern as it occurs at the call site; if no correct seam exists, that itself is the finding — the architecture is preventing the bug from being locked down.

nodes.label: Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 is the skill itself: with a tight red-capable pass/fail signal the cause will be found. Without one, no code reading helps. A 30-second flaky loop is barely better than none; a 2-second deterministic one is a debugging superpower.

nodes.label: HITL Loop Template Script
nodes.rationale: Last-resort loop: if a human must click, drive them with scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh so the loop stays structured and captured output feeds back to the agent.

nodes.label: Post-mortem
nodes.rationale: After the fix is in, ask what would have prevented the bug; if the answer involves architectural change, hand off to improve-codebase-architecture with the specifics.

nodes.label: Minimise Repro
nodes.rationale: Shrink the repro to the smallest scenario that still goes red, one cut at a time, until every remaining element is load-bearing — it shrinks the hypothesis space and becomes the clean regression test.

nodes.label: Perf Branch (Measure First)
nodes.rationale: For performance regressions logs are usually wrong — establish a baseline measurement first (timing harness, profiler, query plan), then bisect. Measure first, fix second.

nodes.label: Ranked Falsifiable Hypotheses
nodes.rationale: Generate 3-5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses before testing any, each stating a prediction; single-hypothesis generation anchors on the first plausible idea.

nodes.label: Tagged Instrumentation
nodes.rationale: Tag every debug log with a unique prefix like [DEBUG-a4f2] so cleanup is a single grep; one breakpoint beats ten logs; never 'log everything and grep'.

nodes.label: Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs changesets/action on push to main so the version bump and release tag land on the main branch.

nodes.label: Docs pages (aihero.dev/skills-<name>)
nodes.rationale: Promoted skills have a human-facing docs page at docs/<bucket>/<skill>.md (docs tree mirrors the two bucket folders); published URL is aihero.dev/skills-<name> regardless of bucket. Non-promoted buckets get no docs page.

nodes.label: Skill bucket taxonomy (engineering / productivity / misc / personal / in-progress / deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Only promoted buckets (engineering, productivity) ship: they must appear in README.md and plugin.json; misc, personal, in-progress, deprecated must not.
nodes.norm_label: skill bucket taxonomy (engineering / productivity / misc / personal / in-progress / deprecated)

nodes.label: ask-matt router maintenance rule
nodes.rationale: Whenever you add, rename, remove, or change how a user-reachable skill fits the flows, re-read ask-matt's SKILL.md and update it - a new skill it never mentions, or a stale one it still routes to, is a router that lies.

nodes.label: Plugin version sync (plugin.json <-> package.json)
nodes.rationale: The repo is its own single-plugin Claude Code marketplace; Claude uses the plugin version to decide when installed users see an update, so plugin.json's version must stay in sync with package.json's. Validate with claude plugin validate . --strict.

nodes.label: Async Loading (Soft References)
nodes.rationale: Hard references like TSubclassOf force load chains on massive assets; TSoftClassPtr/TSoftObjectPtr avoid mandatory load orders

nodes.label: Performance First
nodes.rationale: Tick runs every frame so it should be disabled by default; timers and event-driven logic avoid wasted per-frame cost

nodes.label: UObject & Garbage Collection
nodes.rationale: UPROPERTY tracking by the GC, TStrongObjectPtr vs addToRoot, and IsValid() vs nullptr are the core rules for safe UObject lifetime management

nodes.label: Execution Handoff Options
nodes.rationale: Offers subagent-driven development (recommended) or inline execution with executing-plans after the plan is saved

nodes.label: File Structure Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Files that change together should live together; split by responsibility, not technical layer

nodes.label: No Placeholders Rule
nodes.rationale: Every step must contain actual content because the engineer may be reading tasks out of order; placeholders and vague steps are plan failures

nodes.label: Bucketed Skills Layout
nodes.rationale: Skills live in bucket folders under skills/ — engineering/ and productivity/ are promoted (shipped); misc/, personal/, in-progress/, and deprecated/ are not. A plugin must expose only the promoted set, which spans two buckets, and the manifest formats do not cleanly express a curated subset of a bucketed repo — the original, half-remembered reason a plugin was not shipped earlier.

nodes.label: Anti-Generic Rules
nodes.rationale: Never produce random floating icons, startup gradients, meaningless blobs, messy collages, fake tiny UI, too many colors, or stock-template boards.

nodes.label: Board Composition DNA
nodes.rationale: Curated rhythm across panels — quiet, functional, emotional, technical, atmospheric, detailed; default 3x3 panel system with logo cover, construction, digital application, essence, color, typography, physical, image, and system detail.

nodes.label: Color Discipline
nodes.rationale: One dominant palette: base, primary accent, secondary accent, neutrals; accents repeat across panels; one accent can carry the whole system.

nodes.label: Reference Usage
nodes.rationale: Extract layout rhythm, grid style, spacing, density, logo placement, accent logic from references but never copy logos, names, compositions, or slogans — references are quality training, not templates.

nodes.label: Analog Degradation Effects
nodes.rationale: Halftone and 1-bit dithering, CRT scanlines via repeating-linear-gradient, and global SVG noise simulate physical media instead of purely digital rendering.

nodes.label: Blueprint Grid Layout
nodes.rationale: Strict CSS Grid anchoring, visible 1-2px solid compartmentalization, bimodal density, absolute rejection of border-radius.

nodes.label: Utilitarian Color System
nodes.rationale: Gradients, soft shadows, and translucency prohibited; one substrate palette per project (never mix light/dark); single hazard red accent, optional terminal green for one element only.

nodes.label: Tactical Telemetry & CRT Terminal Archetype
nodes.rationale: Classified military database / aerospace HUD aesthetic: dark mode only, high-density tabular monospace data, ASCII framing, phosphor glow and scanlines.

nodes.label: Web Engineering Directives
nodes.rationale: grid gap:1px razor-thin lines, semantic tags (data, samp, kbd, output, dl), clamp() exclusively for macro-typography.

nodes.label: Brand Strategy First
nodes.rationale: A premium brand kit is a visual argument for why the brand exists; infer category, audience, metaphor, trust level, and symbol logic before generating.

nodes.label: GSAP StickyStack Pattern
nodes.rationale: Must be a REAL sticky-stack, not a sequential reveal list: start:'top top' pins at viewport top (start:'top center' fires halfway through), pin:true, previous card shrinks via the NEXT card's scroll trigger.

nodes.label: Design Taste Frontend v1
nodes.rationale: Original v1 taste-skill, preserved for projects depending on its exact behavior; the current default is design-taste-frontend (v2 experimental), a substantial rewrite.

nodes.label: Emil Kowalski Motion
nodes.rationale: Follow-up skill used AFTER an interface exists: pick the smallest set of motion moments that clarify state or hierarchy - product-grade restraint, not a motion demo. Prefer transform/opacity, one motion language, prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks.

nodes.label: Frontend Design
nodes.rationale: Adapted from Anthropic's official frontend-design skill: commit to one aesthetic direction, design the real interface (empty/loading/error states), avoid generic AI defaults (purple-blue gradients, vague glass cards).

nodes.label: Frontend Dev
nodes.rationale: Curated from the MiniMax AI team; catalogue entry advertising the skill in Open Design - full workflow runs from the upstream bundle.

nodes.label: Flow (main flow, on-ramps, standalones)
nodes.rationale: A flow is a path through the skills rather than a single one: one main flow (idea to ship), two on-ramps that merge onto it, and everything else a standalone.

nodes.label: Spec axis
nodes.rationale: Asks the orthogonal question - does the code do what the issue or spec actually asked, without missing requirements or smuggling in scope creep. Needs an issue reference to find the origin spec; otherwise it skips and reports no spec available.

nodes.label: Standards axis
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the diff conforms to how this repo writes code - its CODING_STANDARDS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md, plus a fixed baseline of ~12 Fowler code smells.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Feathers' term - a place you can change behaviour without editing there; preferred over the overloaded boundary. Callers and tests cross the same seam, so the interface is the test surface. Interface means every fact a caller must know: signatures, invariants, ordering, error modes, performance.

nodes.label: Two prototype branches
nodes.rationale: State/logic questions get a tiny interactive terminal app printing full state after every action; UI questions get several radically different variations on one route. Picking the wrong branch wastes the whole prototype, so the question comes first.

nodes.label: docs/agents/*.md config files
nodes.rationale: The shared substrate the rest of the toolkit stands on: issue-tracker.md, domain.md, and triage-labels.md when triage is installed, plus an Agent skills block pointing to them in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md.

nodes.label: Three setup decisions
nodes.rationale: Issue tracker (GitHub, GitLab, local markdown, or other; proposed from git remote), triage labels (only if triage is installed), and domain docs (single-context assumed, multi-context map only on monorepo signals). Each leads with a recommended answer.

nodes.label: decision-mapping (predecessor of wayfinder)
nodes.rationale: Renamed to wayfinder: decision map was jargony and inaccurate - only one ticket type is actually a decision.

nodes.label: review skill (predecessor of code-review)
nodes.rationale: The in-progress review skill was renamed to code-review, moved into engineering/, and hardened with an always-on Fowler smell baseline.

nodes.label: grilling skill (shared interview primitive)
nodes.rationale: The reusable interview loop behind grill-me and grill-with-docs: interview the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea until every branch of the decision tree is resolved.

nodes.label: User-invoked vs Model-invoked taxonomy
nodes.rationale: User-invoked skills are reachable only when you type them and exist to orchestrate; model-invoked skills can also be reached automatically when the task fits and hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one.

nodes.label: to-spec skill
nodes.rationale: Turns the current conversation into a spec and publishes it to the issue tracker; no interview - synthesizes what has already been discussed.

nodes.label: to-tickets skill
nodes.rationale: Breaks any plan, spec, or conversation into tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges - written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker.

nodes.label: triage skill
nodes.rationale: Moves issues through a state machine of triage roles; uses labels configured by setup-matt-pocock-skills.

nodes.label: wayfinder skill
nodes.rationale: Plans a huge chunk of work - more than one agent session can hold - as a shared map of investigation tickets on the issue tracker; resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

nodes.label: ask-matt (router skill)
nodes.rationale: Does no work itself - it only orients. It exists for the user-invoked skills above all, since nothing fires those for you.

nodes.label: code-review (two-axis review skill)
nodes.rationale: Reviews the diff between HEAD and a fixed point along two separate axes run as parallel sub-agents; keeping them separate is the whole point because a change can pass one axis and fail the other.

nodes.label: codebase-design (deep-module vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: A language, not a procedure - fixes the words (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) so design conversations speak the same way. Component, service, API, and boundary are deliberately banned for blurring distinctions.

nodes.label: diagnosing-bugs (diagnosis loop)
nodes.rationale: Disciplined loop for hard bugs and performance regressions: reproduce, minimise, rank hypotheses, instrument, fix with a regression test. Refuses to hypothesise before a tight feedback loop exists.

nodes.label: domain-modeling (ubiquitous language builder)
nodes.rationale: The active discipline, not the passive one: for when you are changing the model - coining a canonical term, catching a contradiction between code and what was just said, recording a hard-to-reverse decision.

nodes.label: grill-with-docs (grilling + paper trail)
nodes.rationale: Interview relentlessly one question at a time until shared understanding, and write the vocabulary and decisions down as you go. Resolved terms land in a CONTEXT.md glossary inline, not batched.

nodes.label: implement (build from spec/tickets)
nodes.rationale: The hands, not the head - does not decide what to build; the spec is settled and the seams are pre-agreed. Drives TDD, typechecking, and the full test suite, then closes out with a review pass and a commit.

nodes.label: improve-codebase-architecture (deepening survey)
nodes.rationale: Scans a codebase for deepening opportunities and presents them as a visual HTML report, then grills through whichever one you pick. Runs periodically (every few days), scoped to recently-changed code.

nodes.label: prototype (throwaway design answerer)
nodes.rationale: Builds a small disposable program whose only job is to answer one design question. Throwaway from day one - no tests, no error handling beyond what makes it run, no persistence.

nodes.label: research (delegated reading)
nodes.rationale: Answers a question by reading the sources that own the answer and leaving a cited Markdown file behind. Reading runs as a background agent so you keep working.

nodes.label: resolving-merge-conflicts (intent-based)
nodes.rationale: Works through an in-progress git merge or rebase conflict hunk by hunk and finishes the operation - the merge always gets finished, never --abort.

nodes.label: setup-matt-pocock-skills (repo bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Teaches one repo how the engineering skills should behave in it - where issues live, what the triage labels are called, where the domain docs sit - and records those answers as config the other skills read. Run once per repo, before the first use of any other engineering skill.

nodes.label: tdd (red-green loop)
nodes.rationale: Builds a feature or fixes a bug test-first, one behaviour at a time. Will not write all tests up front - horizontal slicing produces tests of imagined behaviour.

nodes.label: Out of scope: mainstream issue trackers only
nodes.rationale: Every issue-tracker backend hard-codes a CLI shape into the skills (commands, flags, output parsing); each new backend is permanent maintenance surface that must keep working and keep being tested against to-spec, to-tickets, triage. That cost is only worth paying for trackers a meaningful fraction of users actually have. Escape hatches: local markdown and other/custom. Prior request: #99 dex backend.
nodes.norm_label: out of scope: mainstream issue trackers only

nodes.label: Out of scope: hard question limits during grilling
nodes.rationale: Grilling is intentionally open-ended: keep digging until each branch of the decision tree is resolved. A fixed cap conflates two failure modes - many questions because the plan is under-specified (working as intended) vs redundant questions (a prompt-quality issue). Natural-language steering is the intended control surface, not a numeric limit. Prior request: #44.
nodes.norm_label: out of scope: hard question limits during grilling

nodes.label: Out of scope: verify/check mode for setup-matt-pocock-skills
nodes.rationale: A separate verify skill or --verify flag would duplicate work the existing setup skill already handles in conversation; the skill is prompt-driven so the maintainer can scope it to a verification pass. Keeping configuration management to a single skill avoids two skills drifting when seed templates evolve. Prior request: #106.
nodes.norm_label: out of scope: verify/check mode for setup-matt-pocock-skills

nodes.label: Fowler smell baseline
nodes.rationale: A curated ~12 high-signal Bad Smells in Code (Mysterious Name, Duplicated Code, Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Repeated Switches, Shotgun Surgery, Divergent Change, Speculative Generality, Message Chains, Middle Man, Refused Bequest). Two binding rules: a documented repo standard overrides it, and every smell is a judgement call, never a hard violation.

nodes.label: Deletion test
nodes.rationale: Imagine deleting the module - if complexity vanishes it was a pass-through; if it reappears across N callers it was earning its keep.

nodes.label: Two-adapters rule
nodes.rationale: One adapter means a hypothetical seam; two adapters means a real one - don't cut a seam until something actually varies across it.

nodes.label: Repro ladder
nodes.rationale: A ladder of ways to build the loop - failing test, curl script, CLI diff, headless browser, replayed trace, throwaway harness, fuzz loop, git bisect run, differential run - and only as a last resort a human-in-the-loop bash script.

nodes.label: Tight feedback loop
nodes.rationale: One runnable command that goes red on this bug. No red-capable loop, no diagnosis. 30-second flaky loop is barely better than none; a 2-second deterministic one is a debugging superpower. For non-deterministic bugs the goal is a higher reproduction rate: loop, parallelise, add stress.

nodes.label: Glossary vs ADR split
nodes.rationale: CONTEXT.md captures language (kept ruthlessly free of implementation detail); an ADR captures a decision with a high bar - offered only when the choice is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. Both created lazily.

nodes.label: Grilling paper trail
nodes.rationale: A plain interview sharpens thinking and then evaporates; this one captures each term the moment it resolves so the alignment survives the conversation. ADRs offered sparingly, only for hard-to-reverse, surprising, real-trade-off decisions.

nodes.label: Pre-agreed seams
nodes.rationale: The stable interface a feature is tested at, chosen before any code is written. Tests target something durable, so the code underneath can move without the tests moving.

nodes.label: Deletion test (candidate filter)
nodes.rationale: Every candidate must pass the deletion test - would removing this module concentrate complexity behind a smaller interface, or just move it around? Only the concentrates cases earn a card; this stops the report becoming generic cleanup advice.

nodes.label: Prototype as primary source
nodes.rationale: The prototype itself is the runnable evidence the answer came from. Once the answer is captured, fold validated decisions into real code, capture the prototype on a throwaway branch - out of main, never merged - with a context pointer on the implementation issue.

nodes.label: Background agent delegation
nodes.rationale: Research is legwork you delegate, not thinking you outsource - you get back a document to react to, with its sources attached.

nodes.label: Primary sources only
nodes.rationale: Works only from official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs - never a secondary write-up - so what it saves is traceable to something authoritative rather than a summary of a summary.

nodes.label: Resolve by intent
nodes.rationale: The trap in a conflict is treating it as a text problem. Before touching a hunk it traces each side to its primary source (commit message, PR, original issue) to preserve both intents where compatible; it never invents behaviour to paper over a clash.

nodes.label: Red-green loop
nodes.rationale: Write one failing test (red), add just enough code to pass it (green), repeat - each cycle informed by what the last one taught. Refactor only once the suite is green, never while red.

nodes.label: Tautological tests
nodes.rationale: A test whose assertion is recomputed the way the code computes it passes by construction and gives zero confidence. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth - a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.

nodes.label: Tracer bullet
nodes.rationale: The first cycle proves a single path works end-to-end before building outward - you never outrun your headlights by committing to test structure you don't yet understand.

nodes.label: Vertical slices
nodes.rationale: One test, then just enough code to pass it, then the next test. Tests target public interfaces only so the implementation can change without the tests moving.

nodes.label: Grilling confirmation gate
nodes.rationale: The agent won't enact the plan until the human confirms shared understanding has been reached, turning the existing completion criterion into an explicit stop-gate.

nodes.label: Facts vs decisions in grilling
nodes.rationale: Facts are looked up (explore the codebase); decisions are put to the human and wait for an answer. The old blanket explore-the-codebase line read as license to answer decisions autonomously once another skill runs grilling in a resolve-the-ticket frame.

nodes.label: Wayfinder fog-of-war map
nodes.rationale: Wayfinding charts a route through a foggy problem: the map is an index, not a store - a decision lives in exactly one place (its ticket), so the map only gists and links, never restates. Fog vs out of scope is split: Not-yet-specified graduates as the frontier advances; Out of scope never does. Destination is the leading word.

nodes.label: HITL / AFK ticket classification
nodes.rationale: Every ticket type is HITL (human in the loop - grilling, prototype) or AFK (agent alone - research). A HITL ticket only resolves through the live exchange, so wait-for-the-human falls out of the label; a grilling agent that answers its own questions has by definition broken HITL.

nodes.label: Negation (steering by prohibition)
nodes.rationale: The elephant failure mode: naming what not to do drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it more available, not less. The cure is to prompt the positive.

nodes.label: Negative space (steering by omission)
nodes.rationale: Blindness to the steering done by what a skill leaves out: every decision a skill declines is delegated to the agent's priors. The cure is to read a draft for its silences and decide each omission deliberately - fill it, or leave it open as a real branch.

nodes.label: Planning skills unification (to-prd to-spec; to-plan + to-issues to-tickets)
nodes.rationale: Spec is the single through-line term (to-prd renamed to-spec). to-tickets breaks a plan, spec, or conversation into tracer-bullet vertical slices each declaring its blocking edges; the one artifact reads two ways - local file (edges as text) or real tracker (native blocking links) - the medium only decides whether anything acts on them in parallel.
nodes.norm_label: planning skills unification (to-prd to-spec; to-plan + to-issues to-tickets)

nodes.label: Teach reuse-first components
nodes.rationale: Lessons are built from reusable components in ./assets/ (stylesheets, quiz widgets, simulators, diagram helpers); the agent reads ./assets/ before authoring and extracts anything new and reusable into a component rather than inlining it.

nodes.label: Wide refactors (expand-contract slicing)
nodes.rationale: A single mechanical change whose blast radius fans across the codebase breaks thousands of call sites so no vertical slice can land green. Slices by expand-contract: expand the new form beside the old, migrate call sites in batches sized by blast radius, contract the old form away, so CI stays green batch to batch.

nodes.label: Instruction Priority
nodes.rationale: User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) always override skills, which override the default system prompt

nodes.label: Skill Invocation Rule
nodes.rationale: Even a 1% chance a skill applies mandates invoking the Skill tool before any response, including clarifying questions

nodes.label: Skill Priority
nodes.rationale: Process skills (brainstorming, debugging) determine HOW to approach a task and come before implementation skills

nodes.label: Five Dev Crews
nodes.rationale: Crews: Developers (dev-build), Design Studio, Game Dev, QA/Review, Ops/Planning - each with its own skill inventory

nodes.label: Evidence Requirement
nodes.rationale: Lint/typecheck/build/tests with real output, always

nodes.label: Plan Before Code
nodes.rationale: ops-planning/brainstorming for anything non-trivial; write specs to docs/superpowers/specs/

nodes.label: QA Review Gate
nodes.rationale: Never skip the gate - qa-review before claiming completion

nodes.label: Team Guide Reference
nodes.rationale: .opencode/TEAM-GUIDE.md defines the 5 crews, their skill inventories, and the work-splitting protocol

nodes.label: Work Splitting Protocol
nodes.rationale: Split work by crew and dispatch via the Task tool; run crews in parallel when independent

nodes.label: Grill the Send, Not the Subject
nodes.norm_label: grill the send, not the subject

nodes.label: Soft-Dependency Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills like diagnose, tdd, improve-codebase-architecture only use the config to sharpen output and degrade gracefully without it, so they reference the domain glossary and ADRs in vague prose only — keeping them token-light and avoiding cargo-culting the setup pointer where it is not load-bearing.

nodes.label: Hard-Dependency Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills like to-tickets, to-spec, triage cannot meaningfully function without the per-repo config seeded by setup-matt-pocock-skills (issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, domain doc layout) — without the mapping, output is wrong, not just fuzzy, so they carry an explicit one-liner pointing at /setup-matt-pocock-skills.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: Explicit /setup-matt-pocock-skills pointer only for hard dependencies
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: explicit /setup-matt-pocock-skills pointer only for hard dependencies

nodes.label: Changeset: Friendlier setup and local tickets
nodes.norm_label: changeset: friendlier setup and local tickets

nodes.label: Setup Matt Pocock Skills Agent Interface
nodes.norm_label: setup matt pocock skills agent interface

nodes.label: QA/Review Crew
nodes.rationale: QA/Review is deliberately read-only (permission edit: deny) so it acts as an honest final gate rather than a co-author; verdicts (APPROVE / APPROVE WITH NITS / REQUEST CHANGES) force evidence over assertions.

nodes.label: Fix Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Apply changes font swap -> palette cleanup -> hover/active states -> layout/spacing -> replace generic components -> add loading/empty/error states -> polish typography for maximum visual impact with minimum risk.

nodes.label: Anti-AI-Slop Audit
nodes.rationale: Upgrades existing projects by hunting the generic AI design fingerprints (three-card feature rows, purple/blue AI gradients, Lucide icons, Inter everywhere, pill badges) and replacing them with distinctive patterns; work with the existing stack, never rewrite from scratch.

nodes.label: Code Review (Standards & Spec)
nodes.rationale: Reviews run along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does it match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?), reported side by side.

nodes.label: Caveman Intensity Levels
nodes.rationale: Measured 65% token reduction. Never invent abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) or causal arrows - the tokenizer splits them the same as full words, saving zero tokens while costing decode clarity. Auto-clarity: drop caveman for security warnings, irreversible confirmations, and ambiguity-prone multi-step sequences.

nodes.label: Caveman Mode-Tracker Hook
nodes.rationale: Stats are injected by the hook (decision:block with formatted stats as the reason) so the model itself never computes the numbers - avoids AI estimation; reads directly from the Claude Code session log.

nodes.label: Prototype as Primary Source
nodes.rationale: A prototype is captured as runnable evidence on a throwaway prototype/<name> branch out of main with a context pointer left on the implementation issue, instead of being deleted once it answers its question — main keeps only the validated decision while the exploration stays findable.

nodes.label: Design Dials (v2)
nodes.rationale: Every layout/motion/density decision is gated by the three dials set after the 'Design Read'. Overrides happen conversationally, never by editing the file. Dial values are contextual, driven by brief inference.

nodes.label: Design Dials (v1)
nodes.rationale: Fixed baseline DESIGN_VARIANCE 8 / MOTION_INTENSITY 6 / VISUAL_DENSITY 4 as global variables to drive layout, motion, and density logic - bias correction against LLM statistical preference for symmetrical, static, airy AI layouts.

nodes.label: Object Pooling Pattern
nodes.rationale: Use when frequent spawn/destroy (bullets, particles); creating objects in hot loops is a universal anti-pattern - pooling avoids GC spikes.

nodes.label: RevealStagger
nodes.rationale: Prefer Motion's whileInView over GSAP for simple scroll reveals - lighter, no ScrollTrigger needed; save GSAP for actual pin/scrub work.

nodes.label: PC Object Pooling Technique
nodes.rationale: GC spikes listed as a common engine bottleneck solved by object pooling.

nodes.label: Web Object Pooling Technique
nodes.rationale: Object pooling ranked #3 in web optimization priority - avoid GC pauses in the browser.

nodes.label: clear_children() API
nodes.rationale: Godot 4.1+ built-in clear_children() auto-calls queue_free; always prefer queue_free() over free() for deferred safe cleanup, avoid clearing in _process, check is_instance_valid() before accessing freed nodes.

nodes.label: Stop and Ask Principle (No Guessing on Blockers)
nodes.norm_label: stop and ask principle (no guessing on blockers)

nodes.label: Verify Tests Before Offering Completion Options
nodes.norm_label: verify tests before offering completion options

nodes.label: Native Worktree Tools Before Git Fallback
nodes.norm_label: native worktree tools before git fallback

nodes.label: Focused Agent Task Structure (Scope, Goal, Constraints, Output)
nodes.norm_label: focused agent task structure (scope, goal, constraints, output)

nodes.label: Question the Architecture After 3+ Failed Fixes
nodes.norm_label: question the architecture after 3+ failed fixes

nodes.label: Red Flags: STOP and Follow Process
nodes.norm_label: red flags: stop and follow process

nodes.label: Iron Law: No Fixes Without Root Cause Investigation
nodes.norm_label: iron law: no fixes without root cause investigation

nodes.label: Iron Law: No Skill Without Failing Test First
nodes.norm_label: iron law: no skill without failing test first

nodes.label: Match the Form to the Failure
nodes.norm_label: match the form to the failure

nodes.label: Model-Invoked Skill
nodes.rationale: Reachable by model or user (the default); the description is model-facing and keeps rich trigger phrasing so auto-invocation fires. The test: could the model usefully reach for this autonomously? Reuse is the reason to extract a skill, not the test.

nodes.label: User-Invoked Skill
nodes.rationale: Reachable only by the human typing its name: set disable-model-invocation: true (Claude Code) and policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false (Codex); the description is human-facing with trigger lists stripped.

nodes.label: Defining Constraint
nodes.rationale: The single fact that makes a skill behave differently from the obvious default (e.g. to-spec does not interview the user again); state it as plain declarative prose, never a labelled aside — it is the most valuable line on the page and must never be omitted.

nodes.label: Docs Page (aihero.dev distributed router node)
nodes.rationale: Most promoted skills are user-invoked, so the human is the index that must remember they exist — that memory is cognitive load. The job of a docs page is to relieve it: orient one reader around one skill so they can hold it in their head. The pages are collectively a distributed router; each is a node, and every link is absolute because the pages publish on aihero.dev.

nodes.label: Leading Word
nodes.rationale: Surface the skill's leading word / defining idea (tight feedback loop, deep module, red-green) so the reader learns what the skill is and the word they will later think with to reach for it.

nodes.label: Blocked Commands List
nodes.rationale: git push (all variants), reset --hard, clean -f/-fd, branch -D, and checkout ./restore . are blocked because they irreversibly destroy work; the verification test expects exit code 2 and a BLOCKED message on stderr.

nodes.label: Installation Scope (project vs global)
nodes.rationale: Scope is a user decision: this project only (.claude/settings.json) or all projects (~/.claude/settings.json), and the hook must be merged into an existing hooks.PreToolUse array without overwriting other settings.

nodes.label: PreToolUse Hook
nodes.rationale: Intercepts and blocks dangerous git commands before Claude executes them; the blocked invocation is rejected with a message that Claude does not have authority to access the command.

nodes.label: fromAny()
nodes.rationale: Replaces double-as (`as unknown as Type`) for intentionally wrong data in error testing while keeping autocomplete.

nodes.label: fromExact()
nodes.rationale: Forces a full object when a test genuinely needs everything; can be swapped with fromPartial later as requirements tighten.

nodes.label: fromPartial()
nodes.rationale: Replaces `as Type` for large objects where only a few properties matter; pass partial data that still type-checks.

nodes.label: @total-typescript/shoehorn
nodes.rationale: Lets tests pass partial data while keeping TypeScript happy, replacing `as` assertions with type-safe alternatives; test code only, never production code — because `as` must manually specify the target type and double-as (`as unknown as Type`) is needed for intentionally wrong data.

nodes.label: Exercise Directory Structure
nodes.rationale: Numbered dash-case layout — XX-section-name/ containing XX.YY-exercise-name/ — keeps ordering deterministic; renumbering uses git mv (not mv) so git history is preserved.

nodes.label: ai-hero-cli Lint Gate
nodes.rationale: pnpm ai-hero-cli internal lint enforces the structure — non-empty readme.md with no broken links, no .gitkeep or speaker-notes.md, no `pnpm run exercise` commands, main.ts required per subfolder unless readme-only — so scaffolds must lint-clean before committing.

nodes.label: Exercise Variant Subfolders
nodes.rationale: Each exercise needs problem/ (student workspace with TODOs), solution/ (reference implementation), and/or explainer/ (conceptual material, no TODOs); stubs default to explainer/ because it is the lightest variant.

nodes.label: Husky Pre-Commit Hook
nodes.rationale: Husky v9+ hook files need no shebang; the pre-commit hook runs lint-staged first (fast, staged-only), then full typecheck and tests, and omits typecheck/test lines when the repo has no such scripts.

nodes.label: lint-staged + Prettier
nodes.rationale: lint-staged runs Prettier only on staged files (fast) with --ignore-unknown to skip files Prettier cannot parse (images, etc.); Prettier config is created only if missing; the first commit doubles as the smoke test.

nodes.label: Package Manager Detection
nodes.rationale: Detects npm/pnpm/yarn/bun from lockfiles (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb) and adapts hook commands, defaulting to npm, so the setup works in any repo without manual configuration.

nodes.label: File Handoffs (Brief, Report, Diff as Files)
nodes.norm_label: file handoffs (brief, report, diff as files)

nodes.label: Implementer Status Protocol (DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED)
nodes.norm_label: implementer status protocol (done / done_with_concerns / needs_context / blocked)

nodes.label: Model Selection by Role and Task Complexity
nodes.norm_label: model selection by role and task complexity

nodes.label: Bento Grid Discipline (rhythm + exact cell count)
nodes.norm_label: bento grid discipline (rhythm + exact cell count)

nodes.label: Commit Subject Line Rules
nodes.rationale: type(scope): imperative summary, ≤50 chars (hard cap 72), no trailing period, no AI attribution or 'this commit does X' filler.

nodes.label: Caveman Compress Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Only natural language files (.md, .txt, .typ, .typst, .tex, extensionless); never modify code/config files; compress only prose in mixed content.

nodes.label: Caveman Compression Rules
nodes.rationale: Remove articles, fillers, pleasantries, hedging, connective fluff; short synonyms; fragments OK; compress cell text but keep structure.

nodes.label: Preserve-Exactly Rule
nodes.rationale: Code blocks, inline code, URLs, paths, commands, technical terms, proper nouns, dates, env vars are read-only regions; anything in backticks or fences must be copied exactly.

nodes.label: Retry Pipeline
nodes.rationale: scripts CLI: detect type, call Claude to compress, validate output, cherry-pick targeted fixes only, retry up to 2 times, else report error and leave original untouched.

nodes.label: Default Mode Configuration
nodes.rationale: Resolution order: CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE env var > ~/.config/caveman/config.json > full; 'off' disables auto-activation.

nodes.label: Caveman Modes
nodes.rationale: Lite, Full (default), Ultra, Wenyan-Lite, Wenyan-Full, Wenyan-Ultra; modes stick until changed or session end.

nodes.label: One-Line Comment Format
nodes.rationale: L<line>: <problem>. <fix>. — exact line numbers, exact symbol names in backticks, concrete fix; never restate what the line does.

nodes.label: Severity Prefix System
nodes.rationale: bug (incident), risk (fragile), nit (style, ignorable), q (genuine question); drop hedging and throat-clearing.

nodes.label: Commit Auto-Clarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Always include body for breaking changes, security fixes, data migrations, and reverts — future debuggers need the context; never compress these to subject-only.

nodes.label: Caveman Commit Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Only generates the message; never runs git commit, stages, or amends.

nodes.label: Original-File Backup Policy
nodes.rationale: Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md before overwriting; never compress the backup itself.

nodes.label: Review Auto-Clarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Drop terse mode for security findings, architectural disagreements, and onboarding contexts; write a normal paragraph then resume.

nodes.label: Caveman Review Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Reviews only — never writes the fix, approves, or runs linters.

nodes.label: Decision ticket
nodes.rationale: A wayfinder unit - a child Issue of a wayfinder:map holding a question whose resolution is a decision, not a slice of a build to execute. The decision qualifier keeps it distinct from an implementation ticket.

nodes.label: Issue
nodes.rationale: A single tracked unit of work inside an Issue tracker. Avoid the word ticket except when quoting external systems, or for a Decision ticket.

nodes.label: Issue tracker
nodes.rationale: The tool that hosts a repo's issues - GitHub Issues, Linear, a local .scratch/ markdown convention. Avoid: backlog manager, backlog backend, issue host. Flagged ambiguity resolved: backlog no longer used as a domain term.

nodes.label: Triage role
nodes.rationale: A canonical state-machine label applied to an Issue during triage (e.g. needs-triage, ready-for-afk); each role maps to a real label string in the Issue tracker via docs/agents/triage-labels.md.

nodes.label: GDScript 2.0
nodes.rationale: Type all variables (var x: int) and use typed arrays (Array[Node]) for performance and type safety; use super() instead of .function_name(); signal objects over string names.

nodes.label: Multiplayer Game Development
nodes.rationale: Never trust the client - the server is the source of truth; lag compensation via prediction, interpolation, reconciliation; design for 100-200ms latency.

nodes.label: PC/Console Game Development

nodes.label: Information as Directed Acyclic Graph
nodes.rationale: Information is a directed acyclic graph — pieces of information can depend on other pieces — so the order of sections and their contents must respect those dependencies; sections are confirmed with the user before rewriting.

nodes.label: 240-Character Paragraph Limit
nodes.rationale: Maximum 240 characters per paragraph forces clarity, coherence, and flow during the rewrite.

nodes.label: Index Notes
nodes.rationale: The vault is flat with no folders for organization; index notes aggregate related topics (e.g., Skills Index.md, RAG Index.md) and are just lists of wikilinks, replacing the folder hierarchy.

nodes.label: Wikilink Linking
nodes.rationale: Notes use Obsidian [[wikilink]] syntax with Title Case names, linking to dependencies and related notes at the bottom so backlinks can be found by grepping the vault.

nodes.label: GLOSSARY.md Canonical Glossary
nodes.rationale: GLOSSARY.md is the canonical language of the teaching workspace — all explainers, exercises, and learning records adhere to its terminology; building it is itself part of learning because compressing a concept into a tight definition is evidence the user understands it.

nodes.label: Glossary Term Rules
nodes.rationale: Add a term only when the user understands it (a record of compressed knowledge, not a dictionary to read); be opinionated — pick one canonical term and list the rest as aliases to avoid; keep definitions to one or two sentences defining what the term IS; reuse the glossary's own terms inside definitions; group under subheadings when clusters emerge; flag ambiguities explicitly; revise definitions in place as understanding deepens.

nodes.label: Decision-Tree Interview
nodes.rationale: Walks down each branch of the decision tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one by one; questions are asked one at a time because asking multiple at once is bewildering; facts discoverable from the environment are looked up rather than asked, while decisions remain the user's; nothing is acted on until shared understanding is confirmed.

nodes.label: Handoff Document
nodes.rationale: Saved to the OS temporary directory (not the workspace) so a fresh agent can continue the work; includes a suggested skills section; references other artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs) by path or URL instead of duplicating them; redacts sensitive information like API keys and PII; user-passed arguments tailor the next session's focus.

nodes.label: grill-me
nodes.rationale: User-invoked wrapper that runs a /grilling session; disabled for model invocation (disable-model-invocation: true / policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false) so the interview only starts when the human types it.

nodes.label: Cross-Referencing Other Skills
nodes.rationale: @ links force-load files and burn 200k+ context; use REQUIRED SUB-SKILL / REQUIRED BACKGROUND markers instead

nodes.label: Description Field = When to Use
nodes.rationale: Testing revealed descriptions that summarize workflow cause Claude to follow the description instead of reading the skill body

nodes.label: Iron Law (No Skill Without Failing Test)
nodes.rationale: NO SKILL WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST - applies to new skills AND edits to existing skills, no exceptions
nodes.norm_label: iron law (no skill without failing test)

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development Background

nodes.label: Token Efficiency

nodes.label: ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`) so simple reads as intent, not ignorance; shortcuts with a known ceiling name the ceiling and the upgrade path so a deferral cannot quietly become permanent.

nodes.label: The Ladder (YAGNI -> reuse -> stdlib -> native -> installed dep -> one line -> minimum)
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: question whether the task needs to exist (YAGNI), reuse what already lives in the codebase, use stdlib, use native platform features, use already-installed dependencies, then one line, then the minimum code that works. The ladder is a reflex that runs after understanding the problem, not instead of it.

nodes.label: YAGNI Scoping Filter
nodes.rationale: The Explore step scopes to where change is actually landing (a named direction, or the last ~20 commit messages) instead of scanning the whole repo evenly — a deepening opportunity in code nobody touches is a refactor you will never cash in, so the report stops tidying dormant corners.

nodes.label: Goal-Driven Execution (Examples)
nodes.rationale: Vague goals like 'fix the authentication system' have no success criteria; write a reproducing test first, then make it pass, then verify no regressions.

nodes.label: Simplicity First (Examples)
nodes.rationale: Complexity added before it is needed makes code harder to understand, more buggy, slower to implement and test; add complexity only when actually needed.

nodes.label: Surgical Changes (Examples)
nodes.rationale: Drive-by refactoring and style drift add unrelated changes; only change lines that fix the reported issue and match existing style.

nodes.label: Think Before Coding (Examples)
nodes.rationale: LLMs silently assume file format, fields, and scope; they must surface assumptions and present interpretations instead of picking silently.

nodes.label: Goal-Driven Execution
nodes.rationale: LLMs are exceptionally good at looping until they meet specific goals; give success criteria instead of instructions.

nodes.label: Design for Isolation and Clarity
nodes.rationale: Break the system into small units with one purpose and well-defined interfaces; changing internals must not break consumers; large files signal too much responsibility.

nodes.label: Spec Self-Review
nodes.rationale: Placeholder scan, internal consistency, scope check, ambiguity check — fix inline without re-review.

nodes.label: Hard Gate: Design Approval Before Implementation
nodes.rationale: Do not invoke implementation, write code, or scaffold until a design is presented and approved; 'simple' projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work.

nodes.label: Portable Logic Module
nodes.rationale: The logic answering the question sits behind a small pure interface that can be lifted out and dropped into the real codebase later; the TUI around it is throwaway, the logic module isn't.

nodes.label: Throwaway Prototype
nodes.rationale: Throwaway from day one and clearly marked: located close to where it will be used, one command to run, no persistence by default, no tests, no polish. A prototype that needs tests is no longer a prototype.

nodes.label: Sub-shape A: Variants on Existing Page
nodes.rationale: Preferred — variants render on an existing route gated by ?variant=, so real header/sidebar/data/density context makes each variant judgeable; only the rendered subtree swaps.
nodes.norm_label: sub-shape a: variants on existing page

nodes.label: Sub-shape B: Throwaway Route
nodes.rationale: Last resort when the prototype has no nearby page to live in. A throwaway route following the project's routing convention, obviously named, same ?variant= pattern.

nodes.label: Floating Variant Switcher
nodes.rationale: Fixed bottom-centre bar with left/right arrows and a variant label; updates the ?variant= URL param so the choice is shareable and reload-stable. Gated off in production builds.

nodes.label: Capture as Primary Source
nodes.rationale: Fold the validated decision into the real code, then commit the prototype itself to a throwaway branch as a primary source (out of main) with the verdict and question-settled captured, so main keeps only the validated decision.

nodes.norm_label: hard gate: no implementation without approved design

nodes.label: State Management Rules (no useState for continuous values)
nodes.norm_label: state management rules (no usestate for continuous values)

nodes.label: Ubiquitous language
nodes.rationale: Challenges fuzzy terms, stress-tests relationships with concrete scenarios, and writes the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. The language and the code are forced to agree.

nodes.label: Deepening opportunities
nodes.rationale: Places where a shallow module (interface nearly as complex as the thing it hides) could become a deep one. Speaks in the shared design vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) and the project's own domain language from CONTEXT.md.

nodes.label: Ports & Adapters Dependency (Remote but Owned)
nodes.rationale: Your own services across a network boundary: define a port at the seam, implement an HTTP/gRPC/queue adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for testing, so the logic sits in one deep module.

nodes.label: Ousterhout's Design It Twice Principle
nodes.rationale: Citation: A Philosophy of Software Design — your first idea for an interface is unlikely to be the best; exploring alternatives yields better designs.

nodes.label: Depth
nodes.rationale: Depth is leverage at the interface, not a ratio of implementation lines to interface lines — Ousterhout's ratio framing was rejected because it rewards padding the implementation.

nodes.label: Seam
nodes.rationale: Term borrowed from Michael Feathers: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place. 'Boundary' is avoided because it is overloaded by DDD's bounded context.

nodes.label: Report Diagram Patterns
nodes.rationale: Mermaid graph for dependency/call flow, hand-built boxes-and-arrows for featured deep modules, cross-section for layered shallowness, mass diagram for interface-vs-implementation, and call-graph collapse.

nodes.label: Mermaid (CDN)
nodes.rationale: Mermaid handles graph-shaped diagrams reliably but shouldn't be leaned on for everything — mix with hand-built divs/SVG for editorial visuals so reports don't look generic.

nodes.label: Hot Spots
nodes.rationale: Scope before you scan — YAGNI. Walk back a stretch of commit history (git log --oneline) to find files and areas that keep coming up, and let those hot paths pull attention first.

nodes.label: Replace Don't Layer Testing
nodes.rationale: Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist — delete them. Tests describe behaviour through the interface, not implementation, and survive internal refactors.

nodes.label: Design It Twice Pattern
nodes.rationale: Based on Ousterhout's 'Design It Twice': the first idea is unlikely to be the best. Spawn 3+ parallel sub-agents each with a radically different design constraint, then compare designs on depth, locality, and seam placement and give an opinionated recommendation.

nodes.label: Deletion Test
nodes.rationale: If deleting the module makes complexity vanish it was a pass-through; if complexity reappears across N callers it was earning its keep.

nodes.label: Interface Is the Test Surface
nodes.rationale: Callers and tests cross the same seam; if you want to test past the interface the module is probably the wrong shape.

nodes.label: Testability Principles
nodes.rationale: Accept dependencies instead of creating them, return results instead of producing side effects, keep the surface small.

nodes.label: Two Adapters Rule
nodes.rationale: Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it — one adapter means a hypothetical seam, two adapters (typically production + test) mean a real one.

nodes.label: Shared Vocabulary Discipline
nodes.rationale: Consistent language is the whole point — use the glossary terms exactly (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) and never substitute component, service, API, or boundary.

nodes.label: Context Map
nodes.rationale: For multi-context repos, CONTEXT-MAP.md lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate — context relationships express via domain events and shared types.

nodes.label: Domain Events
nodes.rationale: Context integration pattern: Ordering emits OrderPlaced events consumed by Fulfillment; Fulfillment emits ShipmentDispatched consumed by Billing; contexts share only CustomerId and Money.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record
nodes.rationale: Only offer an ADR when all three hold: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. The value is recording that a decision was made and why — an ADR can be a single paragraph.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md Glossary
nodes.rationale: A glossary and nothing else — totally devoid of implementation details; terms are defined by what they are, not what they do, with rejected synonyms under '_Avoid_'.

nodes.label: Radical Variant Generation
nodes.rationale: Default 3 variants, cap at 5. Variants must be structurally different — different layout, information hierarchy, primary affordance — not just colour/copy tweaks, or the prototype is wallpaper.

nodes.label: Deep module
nodes.rationale: A large amount of behaviour behind a small interface; depth is measured as leverage - how much a caller or test can exercise per unit of interface learned. Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.

nodes.label: Camera Screen Pattern
nodes.rationale: Hide navigation headers for full-screen camera; flip camera with mirror to emulate social apps; liquid glass buttons on cameras; eagerly request camera permission, lazily request media library permission.

nodes.label: New Architecture Only Constraint (CSS Gradients)
nodes.rationale: CSS gradients require React Native's New Architecture (Fabric); unavailable in old architecture and Expo Go. Also: do NOT use expo-linear-gradient - use CSS gradients instead.

nodes.label: Color API Semantic Colors
nodes.rationale: Use the type-safe Color wrapper from expo-router over raw PlatformColor: exposes iOS UIKit colors (Color.ios.*) and Android Material 3 colors (Color.android.material.* static, Color.android.dynamic.* wallpaper-adaptive on Android 12+). Resolves on-device and auto-adapts to light/dark mode and accessibility settings, eliminating separate light/dark hex tables and colors.web.ts. Wrap values in Platform.select with hex default for web; never pass Color/PlatformColor into Reanimated styles; cast to string for third-party props that reject OpaqueColorValue.

nodes.label: Locked WebGPU Dependency Versions
nodes.rationale: react-native-wgpu ^0.4.1, three 0.172.0, @react-three/fiber ^9.4.0, wgpu-matrix ^3.0.2, @types/three 0.172.0 are tested together; mismatched versions cause type errors and runtime issues. --legacy-peer-deps may be needed due to peer conflicts with canary Expo versions.

nodes.label: WebGPU Custom Build Constraint
nodes.rationale: WebGPU requires npx expo prebuild + npx expo run:ios; it does NOT work in Expo Go - an explicit exception to the default Expo Go-first workflow.

nodes.label: Expo Go First Strategy
nodes.rationale: Most Expo apps work in Expo Go without custom native code; custom builds add complexity, slower iteration, and require Xcode/Android Studio setup. Custom builds are only required for local Expo modules, Apple targets (@bacons/apple-targets), third-party native modules missing from Expo Go, or native configuration not expressible in app.json.

nodes.label: create-expo-module CLI
nodes.rationale: Prefer scaffolding first then building on top; the scaffold sets up the expected layout, expo-module.config.json, podspec or Gradle files, TypeScript bindings, and the standalone example app flow. --name changes the native class name, not the directory name.

nodes.label: ReactActivityLifecycleListener
nodes.rationale: Supports onCreate/onResume/onPause/onDestroy/onNewIntent/onBackPressed; onStart and onStop are NOT supported because the implementation hooks ReactActivityDelegate which lacks those methods.

nodes.label: expo-module.config.json
nodes.rationale: Used for autolinking and module registration. apple is preferred over granular ios/macos/tvos when one Swift module supports multiple Apple targets. iOS modules use the bare class name; Android uses the fully-qualified class name (package + class).

nodes.label: SharedObject
nodes.rationale: Bridge native class instances to JS with automatic lifecycle management; instances deallocated when neither JS nor native code holds a reference; Kotlin cleanup via sharedObjectDidRelease().

nodes.label: Expo Modules API
nodes.rationale: Swift and Kotlin DSL share the same structure; Swift is shown as primary unless the Kotlin pattern meaningfully differs.

nodes.label: Expo DOM Components Codex Trigger Metadata
nodes.norm_label: expo dom components codex trigger metadata

nodes.label: Expo DOM Components
nodes.rationale: Run web code verbatim in a webview on native and as-is on web. Use for web-only libraries (recharts, chart.js, syntax highlighters), migrated web code, complex HTML/CSS layouts, iframes/embeds, canvas/WebGL. Avoid when native performance is critical (webviews add overhead), for simple UI, deep native integration, or layout routes (_layout cannot be DOM components). Webviews have their own isolated JS context.

nodes.label: Native Actions via Async Props
nodes.rationale: Pass async functions as props to expose native functionality across the webview boundary safely; props must be serializable (strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, plain objects).

nodes.label: Router APIs Requiring Props
nodes.rationale: useLocalSearchParams/useGlobalSearchParams/usePathname/useSegments/useRootNavigation/useRootNavigationState need synchronous access to native routing state unavailable inside the isolated webview context; solution is reading them in the native parent and passing values as props.

nodes.label: Config Plugins
nodes.rationale: Synchronous functions customizing native Android/iOS projects generated by npx expo prebuild; accept an ExpoConfig and return a modified version; return values must be serializable except mods.

nodes.label: Mods (Async Prebuild Phase)
nodes.rationale: Mods are async functions invoked during the prebuild syncing phase, unlike the synchronous plugin body.

nodes.label: Local Module
nodes.rationale: Lives inside one app using the host app's dependencies and tooling; skips dependency installation, has no local package.json, no example app, and no index.ts barrel by default; respects package.json expo.autolinking.nativeModulesDir, falling back to modules/.

nodes.label: Standalone Module
nodes.rationale: Own package.json, installs its own dependencies, builds TypeScript during scaffolding, usually creates an example app (default to keeping it; only skip with --no-example or clear user intent); for reuse, monorepos, or npm publishing.

nodes.label: AppDelegate Subscribers
nodes.rationale: Hook AppDelegate events without editing AppDelegate directly; requires the app's AppDelegate to extend ExpoAppDelegate. Result aggregation: didFinishLaunchingWithOptions returns true if ANY subscriber returns true; didReceiveRemoteNotification priority failed > newData > noData.

nodes.label: Module Lifecycle Hooks
nodes.rationale: OnCreate is preferred over class initializers; OnDestroy cleans up resources; OnAppContextDestroys fires when the app context is deallocated.

nodes.label: Expo Autolinking
nodes.rationale: Automatically discovers and links modules with expo-module.config.json; no manual native project configuration needed. Resolution order: explicit react-native.config.js dependencies, custom searchPaths, local nativeModulesDir (default ./modules/), recursive npm resolution.

nodes.label: Module Definition DSL
nodes.rationale: Name sets the JS identifier; Constants are computed once on first access then cached; Functions block the JS thread up to 8 arguments; AsyncFunctions return a Promise and run on a background thread by default (runOnQueue(.main) forces main queue; Kotlin supports Coroutine with Dispatchers.IO).

nodes.label: Expo Modules Type System
nodes.rationale: Primitives mapped across Swift/Kotlin/JS; Records use @Field structs/classes; Enums conform to Enumerable; Either types model unions (up to EitherOfFour); JavaScriptFunction allows direct JS manipulation in sync functions.

nodes.label: Expo Native Views
nodes.rationale: Render platform UI components (UIView / Android View) as React components; use View only when the module actually renders UI.

nodes.label: View Lifecycle Hooks
nodes.rationale: OnViewDidUpdateProps fires after all props have been set; OnViewDestroys (Android only) fires when the view is no longer used.

nodes.label: Expo Development Client
nodes.rationale: Recommended setup for any real or production app; Expo Go is a playground most apps outgrow. A dev client is needed ONLY for local Expo modules, Apple targets (widgets/clips/extensions), third-party native modules not in Expo Go, config plugins, or testing remote push notifications and App/Universal Links.

nodes.label: expo-image SF Symbol Source Guidance
nodes.rationale: Library preference: use expo-image with source='sf:name' for SF Symbols, not expo-symbols or @expo/vector-icons.

nodes.label: Expo Brand
nodes.rationale: Banner design intent: white Expo logomark placed top-left over a photographic background of rolling grass hills under a clear blue sky, signaling that expo-skills is an official Expo-affiliated project with an approachable, friendly identity.

nodes.label: expo-skills
nodes.rationale: Large white wordmark 'expo-skills' centered in the banner with a subtle fade where it meets the hills; serves as the hero/README banner identifying the expo-skills collection of agent skills.

nodes.label: List entrances recipe
nodes.rationale: entering on virtualized-list rows re-fires on row recycling; animate the container once or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow.

nodes.label: Screen transitions recipe (Expo Router)
nodes.rationale: Native stack transitions keep the interactive back gesture and match platform conventions; animationMatchesGesture runs the custom transition in reverse under the finger.

nodes.label: Tab / segmented indicator recipe
nodes.rationale: Sanctioned width animation: absolutely positioned childless pill re-lays-out nothing and preserves corner radius that scaleX would smear.

nodes.label: Toolbar Children Must Be Wrapped in Stack.Toolbar
nodes.norm_label: toolbar children must be wrapped in stack.toolbar

nodes.label: AppClipModule (Swift)
nodes.rationale: Detects App Clip context via NSAppClip in the info dictionary and presents SKOverlay.AppClipConfiguration to advertise installing the full app.

nodes.label: bunx testflight
nodes.rationale: Sets up credentials for both targets; each gets its own provisioning profile but can share a single Distribution Certificate.

nodes.label: bunx setup-safari
nodes.rationale: Registers bundle IDs and creates the App Store Connect entry; its printed AASA JSON covers only the parent app so the appclips block must be added manually.

nodes.label: apple-app-site-association (AASA)
nodes.rationale: The appclips block is what lets a URL on the domain launch the Clip; served extensionless over HTTPS before iOS will trust the association.

nodes.label: Web APIs over Node APIs Constraint
nodes.norm_label: web apis over node apis constraint

nodes.label: Expo Data Fetching Codex Trigger Metadata
nodes.norm_label: expo data fetching codex trigger metadata

nodes.label: Server vs Static Output Modes
nodes.rationale: Server mode runs loaders per request with full request access (personalized content); static mode runs them at build time without a request object (shared infrequent content) and hosts anywhere.

nodes.label: Dual SSR/Client Loader Execution
nodes.rationale: Following the Remix/React Router loader model, one async function serves both paths: serialized into HTML on initial SSR, fetched over HTTP during client-side navigation - the framework owns when/how it runs.

nodes.label: Offline-first React Query via onlineManager
nodes.rationale: Syncing onlineManager to NetInfo lets React Query pause queries while offline and resume automatically when connectivity returns, giving offline-first behavior without custom queues.

nodes.label: EXPO_PUBLIC_ Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined into the client bundle at build time, so they can hold client-safe URLs but never secrets; server secrets need non-prefixed vars in API routes/loaders.

nodes.label: Fetch API Usage Pattern
nodes.rationale: Prefer platform fetch over axios in Expo; always check response.ok and parse JSON explicitly so HTTP failures become typed errors rather than silently resolved promises.

nodes.label: Retry with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: Bounded retry loop with 2^i delay absorbs transient network failures without hammering the server; rethrows after the last attempt.

nodes.label: Token Management with expo-secure-store
nodes.rationale: Auth tokens must live in SecureStore (Keychain/Keystore), never AsyncStorage; single-flight refresh promise prevents concurrent refresh storms.

nodes.label: Collapsing header recipe
nodes.rationale: Never animate header height (layout pass competes with scroll); translate clipped content instead, and Extrapolation.CLAMP prevents inverted reappearing headers.

nodes.label: Drag-to-dismiss bottom sheet recipe
nodes.rationale: Velocity decides dismissal, not distance; onStart captures current value so mid-animation grabs continue smoothly; overshootClamping prevents a gap flash on dismissal.

nodes.label: Keyboard-synced UI recipe
nodes.rationale: The keyboard rides a private system curve arriving late on the JS thread; the UI must be driven by the keyboard's actual position frame-by-frame, never Keyboard.addListener plus a timing animation.

nodes.label: project() momentum projection worklet
nodes.rationale: Decides where a flick was going using Apple's exponential-decay form, so a fast short swipe commits and a slow long one does not.

nodes.label: rubberband() overscroll worklet
nodes.rationale: Makes a boundary resist progressively instead of stopping dead.

nodes.label: Swipe-to-delete row recipe
nodes.rationale: Declaring the pan axis via activeOffsetX stops the gesture from stealing vertical scrolls inside a list.

nodes.label: Threshold-crossing reaction pattern
nodes.rationale: Comparison runs on the UI thread every frame while the JS callback fires only twice per crossing, avoiding per-frame RN scheduling.

nodes.label: react-native-keyboard-controller
nodes.rationale: Needs KeyboardProvider at the root or its hooks do nothing; exposes keyboard height as a shared value on the UI thread.

nodes.label: CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone (120fps)
nodes.rationale: Third-party animations cap at 60fps on ProMotion iPhones without this key; enabling it makes the frame budget 8ms instead of 16ms.

nodes.label: GestureHandlerRootView requirement
nodes.rationale: Without it gestures do nothing with no error; must wrap the app once at the root layout.

nodes.label: scheduleOnRN
nodes.rationale: Reanimated 4 replacement for deprecated runOnJS; belongs in onEnd or a threshold useAnimatedReaction, never per frame in onUpdate or scroll handlers.

nodes.label: Reanimated spring parameter table
nodes.rationale: Springs carry velocity through interruptions while timing curves restart; bounce is reserved for gestures that carried momentum.

nodes.label: Animation Frequency Gate
nodes.rationale: Frequency tier decides whether to animate at all; high-frequency interactions get platform default or nothing, rare moments hold the delight budget. The gate exists to produce zero lines of code sometimes.

nodes.label: Haptics usage rules
nodes.rationale: Fire in the same frame as the visual at the causal moment, one per user action, never the only feedback since haptics can be off system-wide or silent on Android hardware.

nodes.label: Two Runtimes model (RN + UI thread)
nodes.rationale: An animation touching the RN runtime stutters when the app is busy; the whole craft is keeping motion on the UI runtime where worklets run every frame.

nodes.label: expo/examples Repository
nodes.rationale: ~70 with-* integration examples, each built around one library/service. Managed projects (no ios/android dirs), typically a single screen of ~100-200 lines. Mine them for the canonical integration pattern (dependency set, app.json config plugins, minimal wiring against current SDK), not application architecture. Default branch is master.

nodes.label: Example Catalog Snapshot
nodes.rationale: A categorized snapshot for fast triage that drifts; the live repo and meta.json are the source of truth before recommending or scaffolding.

nodes.label: Component Completeness Contract
nodes.rationale: Variant prop over boolean soup, sizes map to spacing/typography tokens, pressed feedback via Pressable style function, disabled/loading handled, style merged last, accessibilityRole set with >=44pt touch target, tokens only.

nodes.label: Design System Audit
nodes.rationale: Measure drift from a single visual source of truth; run the audit before proposing changes, report findings first, apply fixes only when asked.

nodes.label: Escapes-per-100-SLOC Scoring
nodes.rationale: Normalizing raw hit counts by source lines makes audit runs comparable over time; <0.5 healthy, 0.5-2.0 drifting, >2.0 systemic; highest-scoring category is usually the first migration target.

nodes.label: Incremental Adoption Strategy
nodes.rationale: Big-bang conversion produces one huge unreviewable diff and stalls half-done. Create tokens first from the values the audit found most often (an aspirational theme gets bypassed); typography before spacing because it is the highest-visibility win touching the fewest layout decisions; convert one worst-offender completely as reference pattern, then per-screen, re-running the audit after each phase.

nodes.label: New Component Proposal Process
nodes.rationale: Prove the existing component set cannot cover the repeated need before designing a new primitive; if the what's-missing column is empty for any closest-component row, extend that component's variants instead of adding a new one.

nodes.label: Token Coverage Checks
nodes.rationale: Grep-based checks for hardcoded colors, raw fontSize, off-scale spacing, raw borderRadius, legacy shadows, and multiple theme entry points; each hit outside the theme directory is a candidate for tokenization, not automatically a violation (one-off-with-comment exemption).

nodes.label: Inspiration Mode (Adapt the Pattern)
nodes.rationale: Never scaffold an example on top of the user's project. Version-align dependencies with npx expo install instead of copying pins because examples track the latest SDK; merge config rather than replacing it; pull whole examples into a throwaway/gitignored dir for reading, never into the user's project.

nodes.label: Version-Aligned Dependency Adoption
nodes.rationale: Example package.json pins track the latest SDK and won't match older projects; add only the missing deps via npx expo install, which resolves SDK-correct versions.

nodes.label: Consult @expo/ui Before Built-ins Rule
nodes.rationale: @expo/ui renders real SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose and works in Expo Go on SDK 56+, giving best platform fit for sheets, pickers, sliders, toggles, menus, grouped forms. Exception: @expo/ui List is native grouped rows, not virtualized - use FlatList/FlashList for large datasets.

nodes.norm_label: expo design system codex trigger metadata

nodes.label: Component Contract (variants/sizes/states/style)
nodes.rationale: Explicit variants, sizes mapped to tokens, touch states including pressed feedback, and style merged last give predictable APIs: callers may override layout but not identity - a color override signals a missing variant.

nodes.label: Component Promotion Rule
nodes.rationale: Promote only when a view appears on two or more screens, has a nameable role, and its API is smaller than its implementation; wrong abstractions cost more than duplication, so move one step at a time, never speculatively.

nodes.label: Composition over Configuration
nodes.rationale: Content-describing props (leftIcon, subtitle, footerText) proliferate; accepting children with token padding produces components that outlive any prop explosion.

nodes.label: 4-Point Spacing Grid
nodes.rationale: One scale named by size (not use) keeps layout rhythm consistent; snap to nearest step rather than inventing values, and promote recurring in-between multiples into named steps.

nodes.label: Self-Critique Design Pass
nodes.rationale: After building a screen, check hierarchy/contrast, proximity/white space, repetition/unity, and alignment; each failure maps to a system-level fix (tokens/components), not a local tweak.

nodes.label: Static-safe vs Hook-only Colors
nodes.rationale: Semantic/platform colors resolve on-device and are safe at module scope; brand light/dark pairs depend on useColorScheme at render time, so they can only be applied inside components - never mix both patterns in one token file.

nodes.label: otaTotalUniqueUsers
nodes.rationale: Sum of totalUniqueUsers across top-N mostPopularUpdates; undercounts true OTA reach when more than top-N updates are active.

nodes.label: crashRatePercent
nodes.rationale: Computed as failedInstalls / (installs + failedInstalls) * 100; zero when there are no installs.

nodes.label: EAS Update Insights
nodes.rationale: Paid EAS service skill: insights cover updates published through EAS Update and count against plan usage.

nodes.label: Brownfield App
nodes.rationale: An existing native iOS/Android app that adopts React Native incrementally instead of a rewrite; both brownfield approaches preserve the existing native investment.

nodes.label: Expo SDK 55 Minimum for Brownfield
nodes.rationale: SDK 55 is the floor because earlier SDKs lack expo-brownfield and the ExpoReactHostFactory/ExpoReactNativeFactory entry points; pinning the same SDK across the RN project and embedded dependencies avoids version clashes.

nodes.label: moduleName 'main' JS-Native Contract
nodes.rationale: The single registration string ('main') is the only coupling point between the JS root component registered via AppRegistry.registerComponent and every native host call site (getMainComponentName, startReactNative, moduleName props); any mismatch renders a blank screen.

nodes.label: Monorepo projectRoot Configuration
nodes.rationale: When native projects are not nested inside the Expo project, Gradle projectRoot, CocoaPods :app_path, EXPO_PROJECT_ROOT, and Run Script PROJECT_ROOT must be set explicitly or autolinking and bundling resolve node_modules in the wrong directory.

nodes.label: Fused Publishing (Fat AAR)
nodes.rationale: Collapses per-module Maven coordinates into one fat AAR per build variant for remote distribution, while keeping RN runtime/Kotlin/host-common libraries external as POM dependencies so host versions are untouched.

nodes.label: Swift Package Output (--package)
nodes.rationale: Bundles every produced xcframework behind one aggregate package product so Xcode links all of them automatically - eliminating the manual per-framework Embed & Sign step whose omission is a leading crash cause.

nodes.label: Integrated Brownfield Approach
nodes.rationale: Choose when a single team owns native and RN code and wants hot reload, JS source maps, autolinked Expo modules, and one unified Gradle/CocoaPods build; trades a larger build-system footprint for end-to-end iteration speed.

nodes.label: Isolated Brownfield Approach
nodes.rationale: Choose when the native team must consume RN as a plain AAR/XCFramework without Node/Yarn/RN tooling, when teams/repos/release cadences are separate, when the native build is heavily customized (Tuist/Bazel/custom Gradle), or when cheap removal and independent RN upgrades matter. RN ships as a prebuilt artifact with the JS bundle embedded.
